transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. Welcome in—what brings you here to see me today?

Um… hi, Dr. Lee. I guess my mom thought I should come. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything, I just… I can’t really make myself do things anymore.

Mostly I stay in my room, and I know that probably sounds bad. I’ll wear the same clothes for too long, and I don’t really knit or write in my journal or go on walks like I used to. When my mom asks me what’s wrong, I kind of just… don’t answer much. It feels like even talking takes a lot of energy.

I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the right way to explain it.
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way—staying in your room, not doing things you used to enjoy?

I think it’s been… a while. Like, not just a few weeks or anything. It kind of started when I began the community-college program, and that was about two years and maybe two months ago.

I know that sounds like a long time. I guess I didn’t notice how much it was adding up at first.
Over these two years, has this low, low-energy feeling been pretty much constant the whole time, or have there been stretches—maybe weeks or months—where you felt more like your usual self?

I guess… it’s been pretty constant. I mean, some days I can do a little more, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing absolutely nothing all the time, but mostly I just… stay in my room.

I’ll keep the same clothes on too long, and I don’t really knit or write in my journal or go walking like I used to. When my mom asks me what’s wrong, I usually barely answer, not because I’m trying to be rude. It just feels like even answering takes a lot. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um… I don’t know. I haven’t really kept track of it, honestly.

I think my sleep is maybe not perfect, but I’m not sure how to describe it in a way that’s helpful. Some nights I’m just kind of awake for a while, but I don’t know if that’s a “sleep problem” exactly. I’m sorry—should I be paying more attention to that?
Over this time, has this affected your ability to take care of basic things like showering, eating regularly, or keeping up with your community-college classes?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve tried to keep up as best I can, but school has kind of… not really worked out.

I had to stop moving forward in the certificate program. I was supposed to get to the practicum part, and then eventually maybe work in a clinic office, but I just don’t think I can handle that right now. Or plan for it, even.

I don’t want it to sound like I’m just not trying. I wanted to do it. I just… haven’t been able to keep up with it the way I’m supposed to.
During this time, have you ever felt so down that you had thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to be alive?

I… I don’t think I want to answer that wrong.

I haven’t really… I mean, I don’t sit there making plans or anything like that. Sometimes I feel really tired of everything, but I don’t know if that counts as not wanting to be alive. I’m sorry. It’s kind of hard to say out loud.

During these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of time when your mood and energy dropped even lower than they usually are, almost like it got noticeably worse than your typical day-to-day baseline?

I’m not totally sure. I mean… I have bad days, but I don’t know if there was a clear stretch where it was worse in a way I could point to.

It kind of all blends together for me, honestly. I don’t want to say yes if that’s not accurate. Maybe I just don’t notice it the right way.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight—either eating much more or much less than usual?

Um… I don’t really know. I don’t think there’s been anything big like that.

I mean, my eating probably isn’t perfect, but I haven’t been tracking my weight or anything. I don’t think I’ve noticed a major change, unless I’m missing something.
Have you noticed trouble concentrating, like difficulty focusing on a task or making even simple decisions, during this time?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I guess I get distracted sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal.

Decisions can feel… annoying, I guess, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I haven’t really noticed a clear problem with concentrating. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During this time, have you had feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about things, even things that weren't really your fault?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I feel bad about things sometimes, like anyone does, but I don’t know if I’d call it excessive guilt or worthlessness.

Maybe I’m not thinking of the right examples, but nothing really stands out to me. Is that okay to say?
Over these past two years, have you often felt hopeless about the future, like things aren't going to get better?

I don’t think I’d say hopeless… not really. I mean, I get unsure about stuff sometimes, but I haven’t noticed this strong feeling like nothing will ever get better.

Maybe I’m just not describing it well, but… no, I don’t think that’s been a big thing for me.
